correctness.rationale: Multinomial coefficient identity for all integer n>=mh, with nulls; independent proof that truncated Poisson coefficient sequences are log-concave and Toeplitz-TP2, including h=1, m=2, p0=0; strict minor using minimal support s0=(m-2)h; resulting strictly increasing conditional label odds for every p_i<p_j and all n>=mh. Initial uniformity follows from the unique quota-count vector at n=mh; fixed-weight tail follows from an exponentially small missing-quota probability conditional on h-1 appearances of the completing label. Exact-rational test checks 37 full-word enumerations and 87 independent consecutive odds inequalities. No use of finite checks as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The strict all-times pairwise likelihood-ratio ordering for the joint last-label/completion-time law is not stated or implied as an explicit consequence of the inspected unlabelled completion laws: the decisive strict inequality requires a separate Toeplitz TP2 argument and covers all fixed common quotas, heterogeneous positive weights and null draws. Classic generating functions, first-order time distributions and the monotone hazard intuition are acknowledged. An equivalent total-positivity or reliability presentation remains a residual possibility.
residual_risks: Older reliability literature may encode the result as a reverse-hazard or total-positivity theorem under Poissonization; no equivalent discrete multi-quota posterior statement was found.
Some journal full texts were not read; abstract-level comparisons cannot exclude their unstated sections.
Search non-coverage is not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The finding gives a sharp total order, in the likelihood-ratio sense, for how completion time updates the identity of the last quota-completing coupon. This is motivated by inference from a stopping time and unequal coupon rarity; the order holds nonasymptotically over all heterogeneous probabilities, common quotas and null-draw rates. The uniform posterior at minimal time, strict rarity preference afterwards and exponential odds at long times are scientifically meaningful boundary and rate effects not fixed by unlabelled completion-time marginal moments.
